title: UPDATE: Dell Warns 4 Year Memory Gap will Worsen in 2027

tickers.name: SK hynix Inc. American Depositary Shares
Alphabet Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
Production of AI servers is being limited by a scarcity of DRAM and HBM components that may take years to resolve, CEO Michael Dell told the Wall Street Journal. The global memory shortage is a structural problem and is unlikely to see meaningful relief until 2029 or 2030 because new fabrication plants typically take four years to build. Dell Technologies currently faces a $95 billion backlog of AI servers and expects the supply crunch to intensify throughout 2027.

This projected deficit contradicts market fears of a memory oversupply by 2027, which have recently weighed on shares of Micron and SK Hynix. In response to the tight market, Google is discussing long term agreements to secure memory capacity through 2035, while Samsung has already allocated 70% of its capacity through 2031.

Just some words of emotional support for your SK Hynix, $SNDK, $MU fanclub. 

$DELL CEO on memory, suggested: "It's a 4 year problem because there's just not enough supply"

Factories take about 4 years to build, meaning new production would emerge 2029 or 2030.

and that semiconductor shortages could worsen in 2027 stating:

"I do think it gets worse next year in terms of demand and supply". 

I think it's strange we're getting unprecedented forward visibility with memory... as $GOOGL and richest hyperscalers seek LTAs into 2035. 

And a major sector crash as well over durability/financing concerns.
selectedTweets.quotedTweetText:
$GOOGL is now discussing deals to extend their memory LTAs through 2035 from KeyBanc channel checks. 

Samsung already has 70% of their capacity allocated through 2031, and this move would suggest a more durable cycle for $MU, $SKHY, and the others. 

They also expect HBM prices up 80% to 100% in the Q1 2027. 

Having all your capacity potentially allocated out into 2035 via LTAs would ease a lot of memory durability fears.
